args: Analyze the lifecycle ordering bug in GrGpuResource::release() in skia/src/gpu/GrGpuResource.cpp, especially interaction with GrResourceCache::releaseAll() in skia/src/gpu/GrResourceCache.cpp and CacheAccess::release() in skia/src/gpu/GrGpuResourceCacheAccess.h. What ordering is intended for removing a resource from the cache versus invoking virtual onRelease(), and are there analogous methods (abandon, destructor, removeResource) whose invariants constrain the safest patch?

The ASan report shows a GrMockTextureRenderTarget deleted by CacheAccess::release() during GrResourceCache::releaseAll(), then fetched again from the purgeable queue and passed to GrGpuResource::release(), causing a UAF. The supplied diagnosis says GrGpuResource::release() currently calls virtual onRelease() while still registered in GrResourceCache, and onRelease can clear dependent refs (e.g. stencil attachment) or execute a surface release callback, causing reentrant ref/cache mutation and stale queue state. I expect the root fix is to detach/remove the resource from its cache before onRelease(), but need to verify cache accounting and lifecycle invariants, including whether removeResource itself expects GPU data to remain valid and whether fResourceCache must be nulled before callbacks.
